name: Zenas
title: The Lawyer
summary: Zenas was a lawyer (jurist) mentioned in Paul's letter to Titus. He was a Christian coworker whom Paul asked Titus to help on their journey together with Apollos. Little is known about him beyond this single reference, but his title as a lawyer suggests he was either an expert in Mosaic law or Roman civil law.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Letter to Titus
keyEvents.description: Paul urges Titus to make sure that Zenas the lawyer and Apollos have everything they need for their journey onward.

keyEvents.title: Travel companion of Apollos
keyEvents.description: Zenas traveled with Apollos, indicating he was a trusted coworker in the early Christian mission.

keyEvents.title: Context: Paul's exhortation to do good works
keyEvents.description: Zenas is mentioned in connection with Paul's exhortation that believers should learn to do good works and meet necessary needs so that they are not unfruitful.

keyEvents.title: Part of Paul's network of coworkers
keyEvents.description: Zenas was part of the broader network of Christian coworkers that Paul coordinated in his missionary work, along with others such as Artemas and Tychicus.
